payload.name: Verify actual redundancy before skipping candidate
payload.description: Use when deciding to SKIP a candidate as duplicate or redundant; if the related memory pool is empty or lacks the equivalent fact, persist the candidate instead.
content: Before skipping a candidate with reason 'duplicate or redundant', verify that a retrieved related memory explicitly contains the same subject and fact; an empty pool or a non-covering memory invalidates the skip.

When the related memory pool is empty or does not contain the equivalent fact, ADD the candidate (or MERGE into the closest existing memory if the fact is missing there) rather than skipping it. When uncertain, prefer persisting over dropping evidence.

solves: Construction sessions sometimes skip an ADD candidate as 'duplicate or redundant' without verifying that a related memory actually covers the fact, which loses evidence when the memory pool is empty. This rule requires confirming redundancy against the retrieved memory set and, when none exists, persisting the candidate to preserve the fact.
